items.title: Direction Instability in an LLM Evidence Synthesizer: A Pre-Registered Two-Wave Study of Recorded Trading Inputs
items.claim: At research weight 1.0, a temperature-zero hosted LLM flips consensus on about one-third of evenly divided evidence sets.

items.title: Does a Trading Policy Need to Know What It Trades? Microstructure Invariance and Zero-Shot Transfer of Execution Policies
items.claim: Microstructure-invariant execution inputs beat raw features by under one basis point and fail to extrapolate to unseen spread regimes.

items.title: Track or Follow? A Jev-Compatible Multi-Agent Trading System When Web News Lags the Market
items.claim: LLM news judgments correlate with post-announcement returns but the association vanishes from the first trade after publication.

items.title: DeepFinance: Can AI Diligence a $100MM Deal?
items.claim: The top model satisfies only 57.6 percent of diligence rubric criteria and often acts on the wrong inputs.

items.title: Code-Paper Consistency in Economics and Finance
items.claim: Nearly half of sampled finance papers contain at least one potentially serious code-paper discrepancy in a central result.

items.title: Counsel ex Machina: The Value and Limits of AI Financial Advice
items.claim: Users place substantial weight on chatbot financial advice but suffer more behavioral bias under misleading framing.
